caseStudy.problem: Booking a plumber means phone tag and unclear prices. Craft businesses face the same chaos from the other side — requests, crews and schedules on paper.
caseStudy.built: A customer app, one provider app for company managers, their workers and independents, and an admin dashboard — on one Express API and one MySQL database.
caseStudy.role: Everything: product, UI design, both Expo apps, the Next.js dashboard, the API, the schema and the tests.
caseStudy.lifecycleNote: Every transition is checked against an allowed-transitions map and written to a status history.

engineering.decisionsTitle: Decisions I'd defend in a review

d1.title: A booking and a job are the same row
d1.text: The customer's booking and the provider's job are one record seen from two sides — nothing to sync, nothing to drift.
d1.note: Trade-off: snapshot columns keep a booking accurate after a profile edit.

d2.title: 404, not 403, on someone else's data
d2.text: Roles are checked in routes, ownership in services next to the query. A manager asking for another company's booking gets "not found" — existence never leaks.
d2.note: Proof: a dedicated test file attacks it from the outside.

d3.title: Suspensions take effect instantly
d3.text: 15-minute access tokens, hashed refresh tokens rotated on every use, and a user re-check on each request — an admin suspension doesn't wait for a token to expire.
d3.note: Trade-off: one extra lookup per request, in exchange for instant revocation.

d4.title: Bank details never reach the browser
d4.text: IBAN and BIC are encrypted per field with AES-256-GCM. The admin API never sends them at all — only a "payout on file" flag — because hiding data in the UI still leaves it in the network tab.
d4.note: The key lives only in the environment; there is no plaintext fallback.

d5.title: PSP-first, simulated on purpose
d5.text: Designed for a Stripe Connect–style split: store only PSP tokens, never card numbers. That keeps the platform out of PCI scope and out of the BaFin licensing question.
d5.note: Prices are gross (19% VAT); the 12% platform fee is computed server-side.

d6.title: A test database rebuilt every run
d6.text: Jest and Supertest run against a database that is dropped and recreated before each run. It fixed a real pagination flake caused by leftover rows.
d6.note: Guarded so it can only ever drop a *_test database.
